info.title: A2P Campaign Management (10DLC)
info.description:
*These APIs are available only to customers who have been onboarded for the 10DLC Registration Center. They are not widely available to all customers yet. If you are interested in joining the Beta for the 10DLC Registration Center, please reach out to your Bandwidth support contact. Otherwise, please continue to reference the existing [Campaign Management APIs](https://dev.bandwidth.com/apis/numbers-apis/numbers/v1/#tag/10DLC).*

APIs to register TCR brands and campaigns (or to import them if Bandwidth is not acting as a customers’s CSP), as well as APIs to register phone numbers to those campaigns in order to send A2P messages in the North American market.

#### Account Types

These APIs have different behavior for import vs. direct customer accounts. The behavior is always consistent for an account, but reflects where the content of campaign management resides: with Bandwidth, or with The Campaign Registry.

#### Bandwidth identifiers

Some Bandwidth APIs return a `bandwidthId` for TCR resources that have a TCR identifier, such as `campaignId` and `brandId`. Because Bandwidth’s interaction with TCR is asynchronous, there are times when a resource exists in Bandwidth’s systems before it exists in TCR’s systems. In these situations we will return a `bandwidthId` which can be substituted for a `campaignId` or `brandId` where these would be included in an URL to reference that resource. Once a TCR identifier is available and being returned, you can switch to that identifier (though the Bandwidth ID will continue to work as an alternative).

#### Rate Limiting

API consumers may use these APIs at the rate of 3 requests per second, with unused requests “banked” (at the rate of 3 requests per second) up to 12 requests, which can then be used to handle short periods of “bursty” traffic. This rate applies across the use of all v2 A2P APIs, not per API. If this limit is exceeded, the APIs will return HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests).

Athena 10DLC returns the following headers on API requests to manage rate-limiting by clients:

- `X-Rate-Limit-Limit` - the rate limit per second (currently 3)
- `X-Rate-Limit-Remaining` - the number of remaining requests in this second (will be less than 3)
- `X-Rate-Limit-Retry-After-Seconds` and `Retry-After` - the time to wait before further requests can be made (currently one second)

In extraordinary circumstances, rate limits may need to change, so evaluating these headers is recommended.

get.description: **All customers.** Get all 10DLC phone numbers that have been registered for 10DLC A2P traffic under this account, across all campaigns. This is a paginated API that can be sorted and filtered by a number of the fields in the 10DLC records. For example, it accepts a customer profile ID to filter to those numbers that have been assigned to that customer profile.
**All customers.** Get 10DLC phone number details, including information on the registration status of the number with the different mobile network operators.

**All customers.** Get the audit history of this 10DLC number, within the scope of activity occurring for this account. This is a paginated API sorted in reverse chronological order by default, but this can be changed with the `createdDate` query parameter.

get.summary: Get all brands for this account
get.description: **All customers.** Get all brands that have been created for this account. This is a paginated API that can be sorted and filtered by a number of the fields in the brand record. For example, it accepts a customer profile ID to filter to the brand that has been assigned to that customer profile.

post.description:
**All customers.** Pass in the `brandId` to refresh the information about an existing brand in Bandwidth's systems based on the records at TCR. This is useful if a state change occurs in the brand that has not been detected by Bandwidth. For direct customers, this refresh will include related records such as vettings, appeals, and their associated attachments.

**Direct customers.** Create a new brand.

**Required fields by entity type:**
- `PRIVATE_PROFIT`: legal company name, country, EIN/Tax ID, address, vertical, contact details.
- `PUBLIC_PROFIT`: all of the above, plus website URL, stock symbol, and stock exchange. The `businessContactEmail` must be a direct individual address — common distribution addresses (e.g. sales@company.com) and personal or free email addresses are not accepted. Subject to Business Authentication (Auth+) 2FA email verification — the business contact must complete verification within 30 days or the brand becomes `UNVERIFIED`.
- `NON_PROFIT`: legal company name, country, EIN/Tax ID, address, vertical, contact details. Only US-based non-profits (or non-profits with a US EIN) are accepted; non-US non-profits must register as `PRIVATE_PROFIT`.
- `GOVERNMENT`: legal company name, country, EIN/Tax ID, address, vertical, website, contact details. Only US government entities are accepted; non-US government entities must register as `PRIVATE_PROFIT`.
- `SOLE_PROPRIETOR`: DBA/brand name, country (US or Canada only), full address, reference ID, first name, last name, email, and phone number. No EIN is required or accepted. Requires a separate contract with TCR; only available to CSPs that have been enabled by TCR for the Sole Proprietor use case. All `SOLE_PROPRIETOR` brands must also pass an SMS one-time-password (OTP) verification before they are eligible for campaign registration.

**Tax ID format rules:**
- **US:** Nine-digit EIN. Legal company name and address must match IRS records exactly.
- **Canada:** First 9 numeric digits of the Business Number (BN), or Corporation/Incorporation Number, or Registry ID. Name must match Corporations Canada records.
- **International:** Numeric portion of the VAT ID, or primary corporation registration/Tax ID number.

**Identity verification:**
Brand registration triggers an asynchronous identity verification. The result is delivered via the `BRAND_IDENTITY_STATUS_UPDATE` webhook event. Possible identity statuses:
- `VERIFIED`: brand can create campaigns.
- `UNVERIFIED`: identity could not be confirmed (most often due to a mismatch between legal company name and EIN). Campaigns cannot be created. Options: update and reverify (incurs a $4 fee), file an identity status appeal, or request external vetting.
- `REGISTERING`: verification is still in progress; campaigns cannot be created.
- `VETTED_VERIFIED`: brand completed additional external vetting; campaigns can be created. Not available to `SOLE_PROPRIETOR` brands.

get.description: **All customers.** Get details for this TCR brand. The actual details available to Bandwidth will differ substantially between import and direct customers. The `customerProfileId` may also be passed instead of the `brandId` to retrieve the brand details.

put.description:
**Direct customers.** Update the details of a brand, subject to restrictions. This is a full replacement — omitted optional fields will be set to null. The following fields **cannot be changed** if the brand has any active campaign or an active Standard, Enhanced, or Political vet:
- `companyName`
- `entityType`
- `ein`
- `einIssuingCountry`

If these fields are updated on a brand that has no active campaigns or active vets, the brand will be resubmitted for identity verification (incurring a **$4 fee**) and its identity status will reset to `REGISTERING`.

**Additional field-level restrictions:**
- `brandRelationship` can only be updated once every **3 months**.
- Updating `mobilePhone` will change the brand's identity status to `UNVERIFIED`.
- **PUBLIC_PROFIT brands:** Updating `businessContactEmail` revokes the brand's Business Authentication (Auth+) compliance. The brand must request a new `AUTHPLUS` vet to regain compliance (requiring the business contact to complete a new 2FA email verification).

If the brand exists in Bandwidth's system but not in TCR, because we are still submitting the brand to TCR, this endpoint will return a 409 (Conflict). If the brand exists only in Bandwidth's system due to a failure (`brandIdentityStatus` will be `ERROR`), we will attempt to create the brand in TCR with the applied changes.

delete.summary: Delete a brand from the account.
delete.description:
Brands can be deleted once there are no active campaigns on the brand. **Deletion is permanent and cannot be reversed** — a deleted brand cannot be re-activated. All campaigns associated with the brand must be deactivated first. This will delete the brand in Bandwidth's systems, along with the associated customer profile.

**Import customers.** The brand continues to exist in the customer's TCR account.

**Direct customers.** The brand will also be deleted in TCR's system.

post.description:
**Direct customers.** For brands that have not been able to move out of the `UNVERIFIED` status, this endpoint can be called to ask TCR to re-evaluate the brand's identity. This is an asynchronous operation — check the brand history for status updates on the reverification request.

Each reverification incurs a **$4 fee**. Before reverifying, ensure the brand's legal company name, EIN, and address are accurate and match official government records, as mismatches are the most common cause of `UNVERIFIED` status.

Alternatively, an identity status appeal (`POST .../appeals`) can be filed, or an external vetting can be requested to resolve `UNVERIFIED` status.

post.summary: Resend the 2FA verification email to the business contact
post.description: **Direct customers.** Resends a 2FA verification email for a brand that has not completed Business Authentication (Auth+) or RCS verification. Used if a brand's business contact has lost their original 2FA email or if it has expired. This can only be triggered if the brand initiated the 2FA verification process within the last **30 days**. If multiple emails are sent to the same address, TCR rate-limits sending to **one every two hours**. This is an asynchronous operation — check the brand history for status updates on the 2FA email request.

get.description: **Direct customers.** Get a list of the external vettings that have been done for this brand.

post.description:
**Direct customers.** Request a new external vetting for this brand. This is an asynchronous operation — check the brand history for status updates on the vetting request. Results may take up to **48 hours**.

**Supported vetting provider and class combinations:**

| Provider (`evpId`) | Class (`vettingClass`) | Eligible entity types | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AEGIS` | `STANDARD` | All except `SOLE_PROPRIETOR` | Returns 0–100 score; determines MNO throughput tier |
| `AEGIS` | `ENHANCED` | All except `SOLE_PROPRIETOR` | Manual review with detailed report |
| `AEGIS` | `POLITICAL` | `NON_PROFIT` only | Required for Political campaign use case; not available to brands that already have 501(c)(3/4/5/6) tax-exempt status |
| `AEGIS` | `AUTHPLUS` | `PUBLIC_PROFIT` only | Business Authentication (Auth+) — 2FA email verification; required for `PUBLIC_PROFIT` brands to create campaigns; cannot be imported |
| `AEGIS` | `RCS` | All except `SOLE_PROPRIETOR` | RCS Business Messaging eligibility; automatically grants Business Authentication (Auth+) compliance; cannot be imported |
| `WMC` | `STANDARD` | `PRIVATE_PROFIT`, `PUBLIC_PROFIT` | US brands only |
| `CV` | `POLITICAL` | Any | Import only — use `PUT .../vettings/{vettingId}` instead |

**Eligibility restrictions:**
- `SOLE_PROPRIETOR` brands cannot request any external vetting.
- `PUBLIC_PROFIT` brands must have `VERIFIED` or `VETTED_VERIFIED` identity status to request Standard or Enhanced vets (`AUTHPLUS` and `RCS` are not tied to identity status).
- `NON_PROFIT` brands with verified 501(c)(3/4/5/6) tax-exempt status cannot request a `POLITICAL` vet — they already have access to the Political use case.
- TCR will reject a new vetting request if a prior vet for this brand is still in `PENDING` or `UNSCORE` status.

**Political vet additional payload:** When requesting a `POLITICAL` vet via Aegis, an `additionalRequestPayload` object is required, containing fields including `requestorFirstName`, `requestorLastName`, `locale`, `committeeId`, `electionDate`, and `pinPreference`.

**RCS vet cooldown:** After an `RCS` vet completes, a new RCS vet cannot be requested for **30 days**.

put.description:
**Direct customers.** Import an existing external vetting for this brand. This is an asynchronous operation — check the brand history for status updates on the vetting import.

**Import restrictions:**
- `AUTHPLUS` and `RCS` vets cannot be imported — they must be requested directly via `POST .../vettings`.
- Campaign Verify (`CV`) `POLITICAL` vets are import-only; the token is obtained directly from Campaign Verify, then imported here.
- `PUBLIC_PROFIT` brands must have `VERIFIED` or `VETTED_VERIFIED` identity status to import a vet.
- `SOLE_PROPRIETOR` brands cannot import any external vetting.
- `NON_PROFIT` brands with verified 501(c)(3/4/5/6) tax-exempt status cannot import a `POLITICAL` vet.

**Aegis imports:** The `vettingToken` (Aegis Verification Certificate) is required. During import, the brand's Legal Name and Entity Type must match the corresponding values in the Aegis report exactly.

**Campaign Verify imports:** The `vettingId` is the Campaign Verify authorization token. The brand must be a US-based `NON_PROFIT` without 501(c) tax-exempt status, and the token must be unique per brand and CSP.

get.description: **All customers.** Get all campaigns that have been created for this account. This is a paginated API that can be sorted and filtered by a number of the fields in the campaign record. For example, it accepts a customer profile ID to filter to those campaigns that have been assigned to that customer profile.

post.summary: Create or import a new campaign
post.description:
**Import customers.** This endpoint is used to import a campaign if it does not yet exist in Bandwidth’s system, or to refresh or revet the campaign if it already exists. Only the `campaignId` field is required, and optionally the `campaignName` field. If a campaign name is not provided, the campaign’s ID will be used as the campaign’s name. All of the rest of the campaign will be retrieved from TCR. The `campaignName` is not stored in TCR’s system.

The campaign will be associated to this account. A campaign cannot be imported into more than one account (though the brand it is associated to can span accounts). If necessary, the campaign’s brand will be associated to this account (and it will be created if necessary). If the brand is created, it will be created with an accompanying customer profile to represent the brand (the profile can be edited after it is created).

If a campaign is changed outside of Bandwidth’s systems, we will receive notification and update the campaign, however, it is safe to re-import manually at any time.

**Direct customers.** Create a campaign in both Bandwidth’s and TCR’s systems, subject to constraints. To refresh or revet an existing direct campaign, provide **only** the `campaignId` and optionally the `campaignName` in the request body.

If a campaign is changed outside of Bandwidth’s systems, we will receive notification and update the campaign, however, it is safe to re-import manually at any time.

- The associated brand must have `VERIFIED` or `VETTED_VERIFIED` identity status.
- Once a use case is selected, **it cannot be changed** on further updates.

**Required fields:**
- `description`: A clear and detailed explanation of the campaign’s purpose, aligned with the declared use case.
- `messageFlow` (Call-to-Action): Describes how consumers opt into the campaign. Must clearly state the program name, message frequency, potential charges, the STOP keyword, and links to terms and conditions and privacy policies. All opt-in methods must be listed.
- `sampleMessages`: At least **1 sample message** is required for most use cases; at least **2** are required for `MARKETING`, `MIXED`, `AGENTS_FRANCHISES`, `CARRIER_EXEMPT`, `CHARITY`, `EMERGENCY`, `K12_EDUCATION`, `POLITICAL`, `PROXY`, `SOCIAL`, `SOLE_PROPRIETOR`, `SWEEPSTAKE`, and `TRIAL`. Maximum **5** sample messages.
- `subscriberOptin`: **Required for all use cases except Machine-to-Machine (M2M).** If an opt-in keyword is used, `optinKeywords` and `optinMessage` must also be provided.
- `subscriberOptout`: **Required for all use cases except 2FA and M2M.** `optoutKeywords` (such as STOP) and `optoutMessage` are mandatory.
- `subscriberHelp`, `helpKeywords` (such as HELP), and `helpMessage` are required for all use cases.
- `embeddedLink`: Public URL shorteners (e.g., bit.ly, tinyurl.com) are **not accepted**.
- `numberPool`: Set to `true` if 50 or more numbers will be used; this triggers a different provisioning process at T-Mobile.

**Use case restrictions by entity type:**

| Use Case | Entity Type Restriction |
|---|---|
| `CHARITY` | `NON_PROFIT` with 501(c)(3) tax-exempt status only |
| `POLITICAL` | `NON_PROFIT` entity type only |
| `SOLE_PROPRIETOR` | `SOLE_PROPRIETOR` entity type only |
| `AGENTS_FRANCHISES`, `CARRIER_EXEMPT`, `SWEEPSTAKE`, `TRIAL` | All entity types except 501(c)(3) Non-Profits |
| All other use cases | No entity type restriction |

**Special use case access:** The following use cases are only available through prior arrangement with Bandwidth: `USCAAS_LOW`, `USCAAS_HIGH`, `TRIAL`.

**Billing and renewal:**
- All campaigns have a **minimum 3-month billing commitment** (except Political, which renews month-to-month immediately after registration).
- Auto-renewal is **enabled by default**. If disabled, the campaign will be automatically deactivated at the end of the current billing cycle.

get.description: **All customers.** Get details for this TCR campaign.

put.description:
**Import customers.** Import customers may submit a campaign to this endpoint to update the campaign name (if no `campaignName` is provided, or it is set to null, the campaign’s TCR ID will be used). All other fields can be left off as they will be ignored.

**Direct customers.** Update the details for this campaign. This is a full replacement — omitted optional fields will be set to null. If the campaign exists in Bandwidth’s system but not in TCR, because we are still submitting the campaign to TCR, this endpoint will return a 409 (Conflict). If the campaign exists only in Bandwidth’s system due to a failure (`status` will be `ERROR`), we will attempt to create the campaign in TCR with the applied changes. *Only the following fields can be changed after creation:*

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| `resellerId` | The unique ID assigned to a reseller. If a resellerId is entered, it can only be changed to `R000000` to indicate No Reseller. **Once set to `R000000`, it cannot be changed again, and it can only be changed once.** |
| `description` | A detailed description of the campaign’s purpose. |
| `embeddedLink` | Specifies whether the campaign is using an embedded link of any kind. Note that public URL shorteners (e.g., bit.ly, tinyurl.com) are not accepted. |
| `embeddedPhone` | Specifies whether the campaign is using an embedded phone number other than the HELP information contact number. |
| `numberPool` | Indicates whether the campaign is using more than 50 phone numbers. Some network providers require this information, as it necessitates a different provisioning process. |
| `ageGated` | Specifies whether the campaign contains age-gated content. |
| `directLending` | Specifies whether the campaign will be used by a brand that provides direct lending. |
| `sample[1-5]` | Sample messages that are representative of messages sent as part of the campaign. |
| `messageFlow` | Describes how a subscriber would opt-in to the campaign. |
| `helpMessage` | Sample help message that would be sent to the subscriber. |
| `autoRenewal` | Indicates whether the campaign will automatically renew each billing period. |
| `optinKeywords` | A list of keywords a subscriber uses to opt-in to the campaign. |
| `optoutKeywords` | A list of keywords a subscriber uses to opt-out of the campaign. |
| `helpKeywords` | A list of keywords a subscriber can use to get help or more information from the campaign. |
| `optinMessage` | Sample of a message sent to the subscriber when they opt-in. |
| `optoutMessage` | Sample of a message sent to the subscriber when they opt-out. |
| `privacyPolicyLink` | A link to the campaign’s privacy policy page. |
| `termsAndConditionsLink` | A link to the campaign’s terms and conditions page. |
| `embeddedLinkSample` | If using an embedded link, a sample of the link that will be used in the campaign. Public URL shorteners are not accepted. |

post.summary: Refresh a campaign from TCR’s system
post.description: **All customers.** Refresh the information in Bandwidth’s systems based on the records at TCR. This will not update the brand or 10DLC registrations associated with the campaign. This is useful if a state change occurs in the campaign that has not been detected by Bandwidth.

delete.description:
Delete a campaign from Bandwidth's system, starting by deregistering any associated phone numbers on the campaign. If any phone number fails to deregister, we will not delete the campaign. 
Review the history of the campaign to see the status of the deactivation.

The campaign will be removed from Bandwidth’s system. Any associated brand is left alone, even if this was the last campaign on that brand. The campaign remains in the TCR system.

post.description:
**Direct customers.** Sends a notification to a CNP in the upstream connectivity chain to take action on a campaign that has been sitting idle in a review or rejected state for an extended period of time.

The `nudgeIntent` field controls the type of notification sent:
- `REVIEW`: Requests that the upstream CNP take action on a campaign that has not yet been reviewed.
- `APPEAL_REJECTION`: Informs the upstream CNP that a previously rejected campaign has been resubmitted for review.

get.description: **All customers.** Get all phone numbers associated with a campaign. This includes numbers that are correctly assigned and numbers that Bandwidth believes to be currently registered to the campaign in external systems due to provisioning errors.
**All customers.** Get the provisioning history for a campaign. This is a paginated API sorted in reverse chronological order, but this can be changed with the `createdDate` query parameter.

**All customers.** Get the provisioning history for a TCR brand. By default these records are sorted in reverse chronological order, but they can be sorted and filtered using the `createdDate` query parameter. This is a paginated API.

Basic.description: Basic authentication is a simple authentication scheme built into the HTTP protocol. To use it, send your  HTTP requests with an Authorization header that contains the word Basic followed by a space and a base64-encoded string `username:password`. Example: `Authorization: Basic ZGVtbZpwQDU1dzByZA==`.

OAuth2.description:
OAuth 2.0 client credentials flow for Bandwidth 10DLC APIs.

To use it, obtain an access token from the token URL using
`grant_type=client_credentials` and include it as a Bearer token
in the `Authorization` header.

Example:

`Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>`
